newsitem.title: UK: UK govt welcomes jobless, earnings growth fall.
newsitem.headline: UK govt welcomes jobless, earnings growth fall.

text.p: British employment minister Andrew Smith said on Wednesday the government's welfare-to-work policies were helping unemployment fall in tandem with average earnings growth
"By adding to the supply of skilled labour we can avoid inflationary bottlenecks of the past," Smith told Reuters Financial Television
The government's policies, equipping those going into jobs with real skills, would help them contribute to productivity.
"We've seen now across a number of months a pattern of encouraging stability in earnings growth. But there's never any room for complacency here," he said.
"All of our measures together give us a platform for stable growth," he said, adding that the government was determined to keep inflation low.
Figures from the Office for National Statistics on Wednesday showed the number of jobless dropped by 36,500 in June, taking the unemployment rate to a seven-year low of 5.7 percent.
Annual average earnings growth dropped to 4.25 percent in May, from 4.5.
Asked about the level of sterling, up nearly 25 percent in less than a year, Smith said the picture for export volumes "remained quite good."
